description: Miles & More miles, Points, Qualifying Points and HON Circle Points for flights operated by ITA Airways (ITA joined Star Alliance on 1 April 2026; its Volare program ended and ITA flights earn in Miles & More), by booking class. Within one European country and between European countries: fixed miles by class (European Domestic, European Cross-Border); worldwide: distance x class factor (25% to 200%) with a minimum per class. A, F, I, O, R and X earn nothing; E, G and N (Premium Economy) are listed for worldwide flights only. Points and Qualifying Points per flight by cabin, continental or intercontinental (Economy 20/60, Premium Economy 20/80, Business 40/200; HON Circle Points in Business only). Algeria, Egypt, Libya, Morocco and Tunisia count as Europe; set tc to EU or AS for Turkey, Cyprus, Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan and Russia. Miles & More says ITA miles go by ticket price or by booking class depending on how you book, and does not state which bookings earn by price; these are its booking-class rates. Give segs: one entry per one-way flight, in order, with its great-circle miles (calculate_flight_distance gives them) and the ISO country codes of its two airports. Takes no price. Uses cwsi.net's calculator and the airline's published rules. Unofficial.

cls.description: Booking class. C = C (Business 200%); D = D (Business 200%); J = J (Business 200%); Z = Z (Business 150%); P = P (Business 100%); E = E (Premium Economy 150%); G = G (Premium Economy 150%); N = N (Premium Economy 100%); Y = Y (Economy 150%); B = B (Economy 150%); H = H (Economy 100%); M = M (Economy 100%); U = U (Economy 100%); Q = Q (Economy 50%); S = S (Economy 50%); V = V (Economy 50%); W = W (Economy 50%); K = K (Economy 25%); L = L (Economy 25%); T = T (Economy 25%); A = A (earns nothing); F = F (earns nothing); I = I (earns nothing); O = O (earns nothing); R = R (earns nothing); X = X (earns nothing). The letter on your ticket. Business C, D, J, Z, P; Premium Economy E, G, N; the rest Economy. A, F, I, O, R and X earn nothing.

creditClass.description: The booking class letter for creditTo, when it differs from the class question. Ignored without creditTo.

creditFlights.description: The flights for creditTo: one entry per one-way flight, in order, with its great-circle miles (calculate_flight_distance gives them) and optionally from/to airport codes. Defaults to segs when they carry miles.

from.description: The departure airport's code; labels the breakdown.

miles.description: Great-circle distance of this flight in miles.

to.description: The arrival airport's code; labels the breakdown.

creditStatus.description: Your status in the creditTo program, by its name as listed under creditTo. Defaults to the base level. Ignored without creditTo.

creditTo.description: Credit the flights to a partner program instead of ITA Airways's own: united = United MileagePlus (creditStatus one of: General member, Premier Silver, Premier Gold, Premier Platinum, Premier 1K); aeroplan = Aeroplan (creditStatus one of: Aeroplan Member, 25K, 35K, 50K, 75K, Super Elite). Earns by each flight's distance and the booking class at the program's published partner rates; leave creditTo out for the airline's own program. The booking class is cls (or creditClass). The flights are segs (their miles), or creditFlights.

hp.description: HON Circle Points you have this year (optional). Only applies to some choices of the other fields; ignored otherwise.

pts.description: Points you have this year (optional). Used only for the progress toward the next tier.

qp.description: Qualifying Points you have this year (optional).

segs.description: The flights, one way and in order, one entry per flight (1 to 8): fromCountry and toCountry, the ISO 3166 two-letter country codes of its two airports; miles, its great-circle distance in miles (1 to 12,500); optional from and to, the IATA codes of its two airports, which label the breakdown; some airlines also use them (Vladivostok, VVO, on JAL and ANA; the Madrid-Barcelona Air Shuttle, MAD-BCN, on Iberia; the long-haul tables named by city on SAS).

from.description: The departure airport's IATA code, e.g. SYD. Labels the breakdown; JAL and ANA use it to spot Vladivostok (VVO), Qantas to pick its route tables, Iberia to spot the Madrid-Barcelona Air Shuttle (MAD, BCN), and SAS to pick its long-haul tables (named by city).

fromCountry.description: ISO 3166 two-letter country code of the departure airport, e.g. DE.

miles.description: Great-circle distance of this flight in miles.

to.description: The arrival airport's IATA code, e.g. SYD. Labels the breakdown; JAL and ANA use it to spot Vladivostok (VVO), Qantas to pick its route tables, Iberia to spot the Madrid-Barcelona Air Shuttle (MAD, BCN), and SAS to pick its long-haul tables (named by city).

toCountry.description: ISO 3166 two-letter country code of the arrival airport, e.g. DE.

status.description: Your Miles & More status. MM = Member (no status); FT = Frequent Traveller; SE = Senator; HC = HON Circle. Used for the progress toward the next tier. The bonus of up to 50% more miles for status holders is not published as a rule, so it is not added.

tc.description: Turkey, Cyprus, the Caucasus, Kazakhstan and Russia count as. EU = Europe; AS = Asia (outside Europe). These countries lie on two continents and Miles & More does not say which one it counts. Only applies to some choices of the other fields; ignored otherwise.

trip.description: Trip. ow = One way; rt = Round trip. Round trip counts the same flights back the other way.
